wolffish.title: Wolffish
wolffish.subtitle: Runtime behavior. Off by default — turn things on as you trust them.

launchAtStartup.label: Launch at startup
launchAtStartup.description: Automatically start Wolffish when you log into your computer. When enabled, Wolffish registers itself as a login item with your operating system — macOS, Windows, and Linux are all supported. This lets Wolffish be ready the moment your session begins, so you can jump straight into a conversation without opening it manually. Disable this if you prefer to launch Wolffish only when you need it.

blockCredentials.label: Block sensitive data in messages
blockCredentials.description: When enabled, messages that appear to contain passwords, API keys, tokens, or private keys are immediately discarded — they never reach the agent, are never stored, and you get a short notification instead. Off by default so the agent can freely discuss credentials when needed. Turn it on if you want a hard guard against accidentally pasting secrets into chat.

bypassPermissions.label: Bypass permissions mode
bypassPermissions.description: When enabled, all tool actions auto-approve without showing the approval dialog. The amygdala still classifies every action and logs everything to the corpus event bus and feedback files exactly as before — only the human approval step is skipped. Use this for trusted environments where you want full agent autonomy. Disable it any time to restore manual approval.

weekStartsOn.label: Start of week
weekStartsOn.description: Sets the day Wolffish treats as the first day of the week. Drives how the activity heatmap is laid out and how date ranges like "this week" line up in your head. Default is Monday (the ISO 8601 standard most of the world uses); pick Sunday if your calendar app and routines start there. Internal weekly memory files keep their existing ISO-week names so older summaries don't shift.

account.title: Account
account.signOutDescription: Ends this device’s session with Wolffish Cloud and returns to the sign-in screen.

voiceReplies.label: Voice replies
voiceReplies.description: When you send a voice prompt, Wolffish replies with a spoken voice memo. Files and text still arrive when the work needs them — the reply just ends spoken aloud. This switch alone controls whether the model is instructed to do this. Turn it off to get text replies to voice prompts.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.subtitle: Every night, Wolffish reviews its finished conversations — what worked, what failed — and distills the lessons into a playbook it carries into every future turn.

nightly.label: Nightly reflection
nightly.description: Reviews every conversation that has settled since the last pass — automations included — scoring each one and extracting what worked, what failed, and what you liked. The lessons fold into the playbook carried into every turn. Missed fires (asleep, app closed) run on the next launch.

quiet.label: Review after quiet for
quiet.description: A conversation is only reviewed once it has been idle this long, so unfinished work isn't judged early. Anything still warm simply waits for a later night — nothing is ever skipped — and a conversation you continue after its review gets reviewed again with the new turns included.

cards.label: Reflection cards
cards.description: Show a live card over the chat, on this desktop and the paired phone, while a reflection runs. Off (the default) hides the card only — the nightly review and the deep clean still run.

deepClean.label: Monthly deep reflection
deepClean.description: Once a month, a deep reflection takes the opposite stance of the nightly pass: it challenges the playbook and knowledge files against recent evidence, merging duplicates and pruning stale, over-general, or contradicted entries — the structural guard against learned bad habits.

reflection.runStarted: Started — the result card updates when it finishes.

guide.title: What you can drop
guide.skillDesc: A markdown procedure with a YAML frontmatter block (name, description, and optional triggers). Imported as a pure skill — guidance the agent follows when a trigger matches, with no tools or dependencies to install.
guide.folderDesc: A folder containing a SKILL.md alongside an optional plugin/ (index.mjs) and package.json. This is the full capability — the skill, its executable tools, and any declared dependencies, all in a single drop.
guide.zipDesc: The same capability folder, compressed into one file. It's safely unpacked to a temporary location, validated exactly like a folder, then added only once every check passes.
guide.tip: Every drop is fully validated before anything is written to disk, so a failed import can't corrupt or half-install your existing capabilities. The name must be unique across all capabilities, and any system or npm dependencies are installed automatically the first time the capability runs.

howItWorks.step1: The agent takes a screenshot to see what's on your screen — with a crosshair marking the cursor.
howItWorks.step2: It zooms into small targets at native resolution before clicking, so it never guesses.
howItWorks.step3: Every click returns a magnified close-up proving exactly where it landed, and the agent corrects itself if it missed.
howItWorks.step4: This verified loop continues until the task is complete.
howItWorks.step5: It chooses each screenshot's resolution and format itself — sharper, lossless captures when it needs to read fine detail, lighter ones when it's only navigating. Ask for a higher-resolution screenshot any time.

debuggerMode.title: Debugger Mode
debuggerMode.body: Wolffish uses Chrome's debugger API to simulate human-like browser interactions (clicks, typing, scrolling) that are indistinguishable from real user input. This works automatically on all Chromium-based browsers — Chrome, Brave, Edge, Arc, Opera, and Vivaldi. No setup is required.
debuggerMode.infobarNote: When debugger mode is active, a yellow infobar saying "Extension is debugging this page" may appear at the top of the tab. This is a standard Chrome notification and is purely cosmetic — it does not affect functionality. To hide it, launch your browser with the following flag:
debuggerMode.tipText: Create a separate browser shortcut with this flag for Wolffish automation sessions.
debuggerMode.notSupportedText: Firefox and Safari do not support the debugger extension API. Debugger mode is Chromium-only.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.subtitle: Connect Model Context Protocol servers to give Wolffish new tools.

how.title: How this works
how.add: Add a connection with a command (for servers that run on this machine) or a URL (for remote servers). Wolffish connects right away — no restart, no setup steps. If a server requires sign-in, you'll see one button for it here.
how.tools: Everything a connected server offers becomes available to Wolffish on your very next message, in normal chat and to workflow agents alike.
how.background: Wolffish keeps each connection healthy on its own: it checks in periodically, reconnects with steadily-spaced retries if one drops, refreshes a server's tools whenever it reconnects, and keeps every connection isolated so one failing never touches another.
how.offline: If a server crashes or drops offline, its tools quietly step aside while Wolffish reconnects in the background. Nothing breaks, and there's nothing you need to do.

how.pairBody: The QR or code is a one-time offer the organization mints for this desktop. Claiming it signs the phone in as you — no password on the phone.
how.orgBody: From then on the phone talks to the organization directly: conversations, settings, files and usage sync there, and the phone stays current whether or not this desktop is awake.
how.liveBody: Turns run here. A message sent from the phone reaches this desktop over the organization's bridge and streams back the same way — questions and approvals included.

guide.title: Setting automation times
guide.intro: An automation is a schedule heading plus the prompt underneath it. The heading decides when it runs — use one of these forms:
guide.startup: Runs once every time the app launches.
guide.every: Runs on an interval — minutes (m) or hours (h).
guide.hourly: Runs every hour at that minute.
guide.daily: Runs every day at that time.
guide.nightly: Same as Daily — reads better for night times.
guide.weekday: Runs Monday through Friday at that time.
guide.weekly: Runs once a week on that day. Day names are in English.
guide.monthly: Runs monthly on that day number. Keep it between 1 and 28 so no month is skipped.
guide.once: Runs one time at that date, then removes itself.
guide.cron: A full cron expression, for anything the forms above can’t say.
guide.localTime: Times are 24-hour, in your computer’s local time zone.
guide.chipsTip: The chips above the schedule field fill in a correct schedule for you — then just adjust the time.
